name: New York Jets (J! E! T! B! L! U! E!)
commemorates: JetBlue's partnership with the New York Jets (Official Airline since 2009); the team's third JetBlue livery, after 'JetGreen' (2010) and the 2017 Jets scheme, all on N746JB.
description: Fuselage: Jets green all over, with two broad white bands slanting aft round the rear fuselage behind the wing (after the jersey's sleeve stripes), the first from about the wing's trailing edge, the second ending just ahead of the aft door; they run down round the belly. Titles: 'jetBlue' very large in white over the forward windows; the registration in dark capitals with a small US flag over the windows on the second white band, 'AIRBUS A320' small under them; 'J! E! T! B! L! U! E!' small in white under the cockpit. Doors outlined in white. Tail: green fin carrying the Jets' football-shaped logo across it, a white-outlined green football cut by both edges with 'JETS' in white italic and a white jet over it. Wings and tailplane white; wingtip fences green. Engines green with the Jets 'NY' mark in white. Belly: Jets logos (not seen in an open photo).

logos.description: The Jets' football logo filling the fin: a green football outlined in white, cut by the leading and trailing edges, 'JETS' in white italic block capitals across its middle and a white jet streaking over the letters; its foot reaches the fin's root.
The Jets' 'NY' in white italic with a jet streak over it, on the cowling's side.
A small US flag just ahead of the registration over the windows, on the second white band.

The aircraft's own registration in dark capitals over the aft windows, on the second white band.

notes: Measured on the right side only, from one CC0 photo (N746JB at FLL, 2026-03-17, the only open photo of this scheme); the left side is taken to be the same. The photo is three-quarter front from a terminal window, too oblique for photo_trace's affine fit (80 px off), so the side was first rectified with a homography on points of known position (doors, exits, windows) and then fitted; edges are good to about 0.2-0.3 m along the window line, less near the crown. The white bands' edges are straight in side view within 0.2 m and drawn as four-corner stripes; below the wing they're hidden, carried straight on to the belly (a glimpse of white under the wing, about 22.5-26.7 m back, agrees with the second band). The fin's football is measured on the fin's own homography; its bottom reaches the root and is clipped there. Not drawn: the doors' white outlines, 'AIRBUS A320' under the aft windows, the belly's Jets logos (no photo from below), the nose-gear door's '746'. N746JB wore 'JetGreen' (2010-2017) and a 2017 Jets scheme (2017-2025) before this one; neither is in the dataset. Still current: the Commons photo is six months after the unveiling, and the 2017 scheme it replaced was the same jet.
